en.commentary:
I rank the Greenworks BL60L512 first, and a single point decides it. Consumer Reports scored the $769 EGO LBPX8004-2 backpack an 86 out of 100 in its 2026 battery blower test, the highest of the nine machines it ran. The $250 Greenworks handheld scored 85. One point separates the results and $519 separates the price tags. For a homeowner clearing a quarter acre of maple leaves twice a week in October, that gap settles the whole decision.

The spec most people read wrong is MPH. Marketing leads with air speed because it sounds like force, and CFM is what actually moves a wet pile off a lawn. Air volume lifts and carries the material; air speed breaks it loose from turf. You want both numbers to be strong, and a listing that shows a big MPH figure next to a modest CFM figure describes a machine that feels impressive on dry pavement and gives up on a wet October lawn. The EGO LB7654 pairs 765 CFM with 200 MPH, and that combination is why it still holds the handheld performance crown at $329.

Runtime is the second thing to plan around. Backpack machines on their top setting drain a pack fast, which is why both the EGO and the Ryobi ship with large batteries. Budget for a spare on day one.

The choice that outlives the blower is the battery platform. EGO 56V ARC, Greenworks 60V, Ryobi 40V, Toro Flex-Force and DeWalt FlexVolt are mutually incompatible, so the blower you buy today decides which trimmer, chainsaw and mower you buy for the next decade. I weight that heavily in the scores.

One more force is pushing the whole category: California's AB 1346 ended retail sale of new gas leaf blowers and other small off-road engines statewide in 2024. The replacement wave is already running, and battery development is moving with it.

highlights.title: The $250 Greenworks Lands Within One Point of the $769 EGO Backpack
highlights.body: Consumer Reports ran nine battery blowers for 2026 and gave the EGO LBPX8004-2 backpack an 86, the highest score in the group, with the Greenworks BL60L512 handheld right behind at 85. The Greenworks earns that score with 700 CFM, fast clearing of debris embedded in turf, and a noise level low enough that CR noted hearing protection is optional. At $250 with a 5.0Ah battery and rapid charger in the box, it delivers the performance a homeowner actually uses for a third of the backpack's price. That is why it takes the top spot here.

highlights.title: CFM Is the Number That Moves Wet Leaves
highlights.body: Air speed in MPH gets the headline on every box, and air volume in CFM determines how much material a blower carries per second. Volume is what pushes a soaked October pile across a lawn in one pass, while speed is what pries flattened leaves and grass clippings off the turf underneath. The machines I rank highest deliver both: the EGO LB7654 at 765 CFM and 200 MPH, the Ryobi backpack at 850 CFM and 180 MPH, the Greenworks at 700 CFM and 170 MPH. When you compare two models, multiply the numbers rather than reading the larger one.

highlights.title: You Are Buying a Battery Platform for the Next Decade
highlights.body: EGO 56V ARC, Greenworks 60V, Ryobi 40V, Toro Flex-Force, DeWalt FlexVolt and Makita 18V X2 LXT all use their own pack format, and none of them interchange. The blower is usually a household's first tool on the platform, and every trimmer, chainsaw, mower and pressure washer bought afterward tends to follow it. Makita's LXT line spans more than 300 tools on one battery, DeWalt's FlexVolt packs step down to run the entire 20V MAX range, and EGO's 56V system covers a full yard lineup. Pick the ecosystem you want to live in and the blower decision gets much simpler.

highlights.title: Backpack Blowers Earn Their Price Above Half an Acre
highlights.body: The EGO LBPX8004-2 at 800 CFM and the Ryobi RY40HPLB02K at 850 CFM move volume that no handheld matches, and they carry their weight on your shoulders instead of your forearm, which matters once a session runs past twenty minutes. That advantage shows up on large lots with mature trees. The Ryobi is the better buy of the two at $629, coming in $140 under the EGO while scoring an 83 in CR testing, weighing 22 pounds, and shipping with an 8.0Ah pack and a five-year warranty.

highlights.title: California's AB 1346 Turned Battery Into the Default
highlights.body: California ended retail sale of new gas leaf blowers and other small off-road engines rated at or below 19 kilowatts starting in 2024 under AB 1346, and cities including Oakland and Palo Alto layer their own use restrictions on top. Manufacturers responded by pushing their engineering budgets into battery platforms, which is why an 800 CFM cordless backpack now exists at all. Anyone still running a gas handheld is holding a tool with a shrinking service and parts network, and the current battery machines match the output they are used to.

zh-tw.commentary:
我把 Greenworks BL60L512 放第一，理由就是一分。Consumer Reports 2026 年電池吹葉機實測，售價 769 美元的 EGO LBPX8004-2 背負機拿 86 分，是九台裡最高分；售價 250 美元的 Greenworks 手持機拿 85 分。成績差一分，價差換算台幣超過一萬六。老實說，對大多數人來說這題到這裡就結束了。

台灣沒有美國那種整季落葉，但這類機器在這裡的用法其實很固定。洗完車吹車縫、後照鏡、輪圈裡的積水，頂樓跟陽台清落葉灰塵，店面或工地收工前把地面掃乾淨，這些場景真正吃的是風量。

規格表上大家最先看的 MPH 是風速，講白了，把濕掉黏在地上的落葉整片推走，靠的是 CFM 風量。風量負責把東西一路帶走，風速負責把它從地面或草皮上掀起來，兩個數字都要夠才算好機器。EGO LB7654 用 765 CFM 配 200 MPH，兩邊都給滿，這就是它在一萬出頭價位還坐穩手持性能標竿的原因。

第二件要先想清楚的是續航。背負機開最大檔，電量掉得比想像中快，EGO 跟 Ryobi 都配大電池就是因為這個。買機器的時候順手加一顆電池，這筆錢真的省不得。

真正會跟著你十年的是電池平台。EGO 56V ARC、Greenworks 60V、Ryobi 40V、Toro Flex-Force、DeWalt FlexVolt 彼此完全不通用，今天挑哪台吹葉機，等於順手決定了未來的割草機、鏈鋸、修枝機要買哪一家。這個權重我在評分裡給得很重。

最後一個大方向，加州 AB 1346 從 2024 年起全面禁止新款汽油吹葉機在州內零售，整個戶外電動工具的換機潮已經開跑，電池機的迭代速度只會越來越快。

highlights.title: 八千有找的 Greenworks，只輸兩萬四的 EGO 背負機一分
highlights.body: Consumer Reports 2026 年實測跑了九台電池吹葉機，EGO LBPX8004-2 背負機拿到全場最高的 86 分，Greenworks BL60L512 手持機以 85 分緊追在後。Greenworks 這 85 分是靠 700 CFM 的風量、把卡進草皮的碎屑快速清掉的實測表現，加上 CR 特別註記音量低到可以不戴耳罩換來的。換算台幣不到八千就附 5.0Ah 電池跟快充，一般家庭真正會用到的性能它全都給了，價格只有背負機的三分之一。這就是我把它放第一的理由。

highlights.title: 決定濕葉推不推得動的是 CFM
highlights.body: 每個包裝盒上最大的字都是 MPH 風速，但決定一秒能帶走多少東西的是 CFM 風量。風量負責把一整堆吸飽水的落葉一次推過去，風速負責把壓平黏在地面的葉子跟草屑掀起來。我排前面的機種兩邊數字都好看，EGO LB7654 是 765 CFM 配 200 MPH，Ryobi 背負機是 850 CFM 配 180 MPH，Greenworks 是 700 CFM 配 170 MPH。比較兩台的時候，把兩個數字一起看，會比只挑大的那個準得多。

highlights.title: 你買的其實是未來十年的電池平台
highlights.body: EGO 56V ARC、Greenworks 60V、Ryobi 40V、Toro Flex-Force、DeWalt FlexVolt、Makita 18V X2 LXT，各家電池規格全部自成一套，沒有一組能互換。吹葉機通常是一個家庭在某個平台上的第一支工具，後面的修枝機、鏈鋸、割草機、高壓清洗機幾乎都會跟著同一家走。Makita 的 LXT 一顆電池能跨 300 種以上的工具，DeWalt 的 FlexVolt 電池可以降壓餵整條 20V MAX 產品線，EGO 的 56V 則有完整的庭院工具陣容。先想清楚要住進哪個生態系，吹葉機這題就好選很多。

highlights.title: 背負式的價格要有一定面積才划算
highlights.body: EGO LBPX8004-2 的 800 CFM 跟 Ryobi RY40HPLB02K 的 850 CFM，是手持機構造上追不到的風量等級，而且重量落在肩膀而非前臂上，作業一超過二十分鐘差別就很明顯。這個優勢在有大院子跟成排大樹的環境才會完全發揮出來。兩台裡我推 Ryobi，629 美元比 EGO 便宜 140 美元，CR 給 83 分，整機約 10 公斤，附 8.0Ah 電池跟五年保固。

highlights.title: 加州 AB 1346 讓電池機直接變成預設選項
highlights.body: 加州依 AB 1346 從 2024 年起禁止 19 千瓦以下的新款汽油吹葉機與其他小型非道路引擎在州內零售，奧克蘭、帕羅奧圖等城市還額外加上使用時段的限制。廠商的反應是把研發預算全部壓到電池平台上，800 CFM 的無線背負機能出現就是這股力量推出來的。現在還在用汽油手持機的人，手上這支工具的維修跟零件供應網只會越縮越小，而現在的電池機種輸出已經追得上他們習慣的水準。

en.commentary:
Ryobi's Whisper Series backpack moves to 8.8 today on two numbers that landed this week. It produces 730 CFM at 165 MPH and runs at 59 dB in whisper mode, and it sells for $199 with a battery included. That combination is unusual. Sixty decibels is roughly conversation volume, which means you can run this at 7am on a Saturday without becoming the reason your street has a group chat about you. Noise goes to 9.0 and value to 8.4.

The Greenworks Pro 60V BL60L512 keeps first place. It delivers 700 CFM with the best balance of weight, runtime and price on this board, and value at 9.5 is the highest score I give here. For a quarter-acre lot with mature trees, this is the blower I would buy without thinking about it further.

The EGO Commercial 800 CFM backpack stays second on raw capability. Eight hundred CFM moves wet, matted leaves that lighter machines just rearrange, and runtime at 9.3 reflects the larger pack batteries. It costs what it costs, and value at 7.4 is honest about that.

I nudged the EGO LB7654 to 9.4 on power. Confirmed testing has it at 765 CFM in turbo and 200 MPH air speed, which is the highest tip speed among the handhelds here, and it clears gravel and caked grass clippings that stall lower-velocity units.

One structural point on platform scores: Greenworks runs 60V and 80V, EGO runs 56V, Ryobi runs 40V. Higher voltage delivers more consistent power under sustained load. Pick the platform before the tool, because the batteries are where your money ends up.

highlights.title: 59 dB at $199 with a battery is the value story of the season
highlights.body: Ryobi's Whisper Series runs at roughly conversation volume while moving 730 CFM, and it ships with a battery at $199. Noise ordinances and neighbors are the real constraint on when you can do yard work, so a blower quiet enough for early Saturday morning is a blower with more usable hours. That takes noise to 9.0 and value to 8.4.

highlights.title: Greenworks BL60L512 is the default recommendation
highlights.body: Seven hundred CFM with the best weight-to-runtime-to-price balance on this board, and the highest value score here at 9.5. For a typical suburban lot with mature trees, nothing else on this list gives you more finished yard per dollar. It stays at number one for the fourth week running.

highlights.title: Eight hundred CFM is what wet leaves require
highlights.body: Matted, rain-soaked leaf litter needs volume rather than velocity to lift, and the EGO Commercial backpack's 800 CFM is the number that does it. Runtime at 9.3 comes from the larger backpack cells. If your fall cleanup happens after the rain rather than before it, this is the machine that finishes the job.

highlights.title: Choose the battery platform first
highlights.body: Greenworks at 60V and 80V, EGO at 56V and Ryobi at 40V all hold voltage differently under sustained load, and higher voltage generally means steadier power. More importantly, your next five tools will share those packs. The blower is a one-time decision, the platform is a five-year one.

Look at both figures together, and treat any manufacturer quoting only one as having chosen the flattering number.

One note on platform. If you already own batteries from a tool brand, buying a bare tool on that platform costs far less than a new kit. Check platform compatibility before you compare complete kits.
